lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD hammer prices at Gowans (no asking or unsold evidence found). Gold-clasp pearl strands made $80 to $340 hammer in the last 12 months (9 close lots, median about $120 to $130); none had an 18ct clasp or 10mm+ pearls stated, so pearl quality of the comparables is unknown. No currency conversion.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = $80 hammer (lot 419440). Treated as a hammer-equivalent value; $80 / 1.198 = $66.78, rounded down to $65. Flip: likely resale about $130 (median of close gold-clasp sales). Less about 13% selling fees (eBay-style) = $113.10, less $10 outbound post = $103.10; / 2.396 = $43.03, rounded down to $40. Melt: 18ct clasp is likely under 1g; at 0.75 purity it is a small add-on, not weighed, so no melt figure (spot price pages were not reachable). Pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: 750 mark read on the clasp and 9 opened Gowans SOLD results, but they are close rather than the same item (pearl size, type and quality unknown), and the pearls themselves are unverified.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: even round cream pearls, roughly 10mm, about 43 to 45 on the strand, moderate lustre, slight pinkish overtone, a few look slightly off-round. Photo 2 (enlarged): bolt-ring clasp clearly stamped 750; a short twisted gold wire/chain section attaches the clasp, which is unusual and worth checking. Knotting between pearls not visible.
lots.condition: Looks clean in the photos; knotting, thread condition, drill holes and pearl surface blemishes cannot be judged.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are the pearls genuine (tooth test or drill-hole check)? Is the strand knotted and is the thread sound? What is the strand length and are the pearls really 10.5mm? Is the gold section attached to the 750 clasp also gold? Any paperwork for the 'South Seas' claim?
